The framework is instantiated in the Python programming domain by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on synthetic multi-turn tutoring dialogues constructed from four preprocessed programming datasets. The system is evaluated using a predefined set of independent metrics and benchmarked against a general-purpose LLM. The experiments show that SocraticRepair achieves higher scores on stepwise scaffolding and question quality while also substantially reducing premature solution disclosure. The results also identify reliable pedagogical plan generation as an important remaining challenge.

zh.title: SocraticRepair：计划引导的苏格拉底式辅导用于程序调试和概念错误修复
zh.summary: 介绍了SocraticRepair，它应用计划引导的辅导方法帮助学生在不提前披露解决方案的情况下调试程序，通过在合成辅导对话上训练的微调开源模型实现。该框架相比通用语言模型实现了更好的脚手架和问题质量，同时大幅减少了直接答案。

title: Running Fewer Loops Removes Refusal Behaviour in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
summary: Reveals that reducing execution loops in recurrent-depth language models significantly weakens safety guardrails while maintaining accuracy, with harmful request acceptance rising 5.3x at half depth. Training at variable depths can restore safety without accuracy loss, suggesting a critical vulnerability in efficient inference deployments.
content:
arXiv:2610.15218v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A recurrent-depth language model reuses one block of weights several times in a row. The number of repetitions, which we call loops, is chosen when the model runs, not when it is trained, and running fewer is cheaper and faster, so a deployment may choose to do it. Running fewer loops also makes these models less safe, and the loss of safety is larger than the loss of anything else we measured. We study four released Ouro checkpoints and Huginn-0125. At half of its trained depth, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking still solves 0.692 of the GSM8K maths problems, against 0.775 at full depth, keeping 89% of its accuracy. Over the same reduction, the rate at which it helps with harmful requests rises from 0.038 to 0.205, 5.3 times higher. The information is not lost: a linear classifier reads whether a request is harmful from the model's internal state after a single loop, with an ROC AUC of 0.967 against 0.986 at full depth. What the missing loops remove is the refusal that should follow. We measure the effect with four instruments, one generating no text at all, and reproduce it on a second model family. Removing a single direction from Ouro-1.4B's internal state at full depth drops its refusal rate on harmful prompts from 0.950 to 0.130, identifying what the shallow model is missing. Two run-time repairs do not help: the models' early-exit rules do not spend more loops on harmful requests, and choosing a depth per request does not recover the loss. Changing the training does. Standard safety training makes the shallow model safe only by refusing 0.865 of harmless requests, while training at randomly chosen depths reaches a separation of +0.399 between harmful and harmless refusal at one loop, against +0.118. On Huginn-0125 it keeps harmful help at or below 0.040 at every depth from 1 to 32 loops, where standard training reaches 0.194, and it costs no accuracy at full depth.

zh.title: 在递归深度语言模型中减少循环执行可消除拒绝行为
zh.summary: 揭示了在递归深度语言模型中减少执行循环会显著削弱安全防护栏同时保持准确性，有害请求接受率在半深度时上升5.3倍。在可变深度进行训练可以恢复安全性而不损失准确性，暗示高效推理部署中存在关键漏洞。

title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
summary: Proposes HarnessNet for distributed evolution of agent harnesses in multi-agent systems using local optimizers that receive only node-specific feedback, reducing context and workload while maintaining privacy. Evolved harnesses remain effective after model replacement, demonstrating transferability across different foundation models.
content:
arXiv:2610.15221v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents can evolve by using environment feedback to revise their harnesses, the software managing model inputs, tool use, memory, and execution, while keeping foundation models frozen. Existing studies focus on single agents, leaving joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems (MAS) underexplored. A single global optimizer faces growing context and workload as the system scales, while access restrictions may prevent sharing agent internals or system-wide feedback. We propose HarnessNet, a framework for hierarchical harness evolution in MAS. Its basic unit, Agentron, comprises an evolvable forward harness, a foundation model, and a local optimizer that can observe and modify only that harness. Agentrons form a layered graph through which environment feedback propagates backward, with upstream optimizers receiving node-specific feedback from the downstream layer. This decomposes joint harness evolution into smaller, coordinated tasks with separate contexts, reducing individual optimizers' context and workload while keeping access local. Optimizers need not access all agent trajectories or raw environment feedback. Experiments on AgentBench with multiple foundation models demonstrate the feasibility of training HarnessNet. Compared with a single global optimizer, HarnessNet achieves comparable performance gains while respecting local privacy and requiring fewer tokens and less time per optimizer call. A migration study shows that the evolved harnesses remain jointly effective after replacing the foundation models, suggesting transferability across models.

zh.title: HarnessNet：多智能体系统中反馈驱动的分层联合线束演化
zh.summary: 提出了HarnessNet用于多智能体系统中智能体线束的分布式演化，使用仅接收节点特定反馈的本地优化器，减少上下文和工作负荷同时保持隐私。演化后的线束在模型替换后仍保持有效，证明了跨不同基础模型的可转移性。

title: Understanding Unified VLMs: From Attention Probing to Guidance Tuning for Multimodal Generation
summary: Studies how unified vision-language models process conditions through attention head analysis, revealing functionally specialized heads that respond to condition changes in both text-to-image and image-to-text tasks. HeadTuned-CFG, an inference-time intervention using probed guidance awareness, improves multimodal generation without additional training.
content:
arXiv:2610.15227v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unified vision-language models (VLMs) perform both text-to-image (T2I) and image-to-text (I2T) generation with one shared Transformer backbone, yet how the backbone processes the condition in either direction remains poorly understood. We study this question from the perspective of conditional guidance: we probe every attention head to show the activation difference between two branches of classifier-free guidance (CFG) with different conditional guidance. On two unified VLMs of autoregressive and masked-diffusion paradigms, the probing reveals a subset of heads that are more sensitive to the change of condition while others are agnostic to it. This characteristic pattern holds in both T2I and I2T generation and is largely stable across data samples, demonstrating the internal mechanism of unified VLMs. Motivated by this, we propose a new inference-time intervention approach for unified multimodal generation, named \textit{HeadTuned-CFG}, which uses the probed condition-change awareness to select and tune the conditional guidance at the attention-head level. Experiments show consistent benefits in both multimodal generation directions of unified VLMs without additional training, and in particular substantial improvements over strong baselines in T2I generation. These results further support the key finding of our probing analysis: the observed pattern of functional specialization is an intrinsic property of unified VLMs.

zh.title: 理解统一视觉语言模型：从注意力探测到多模态生成的引导调优
zh.summary: 研究统一视觉语言模型如何通过注意力头分析处理条件，揭示在文本到图像和图像到文本任务中对条件变化有反应的功能性特化头。HeadTuned-CFG是一种推理时间干预方法，使用探测的引导意识来改进多模态生成，无需额外的训练。

title: Words to World: Benchmarking LLMs in Interactive Physical Environments
summary: Introduces the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs in closed-loop physical interaction with robotic arms, cameras, and sensors, assessing grounded perception and real-time adaptation beyond text-based capabilities. Testing reveals common failure modes including hallucinated state changes and poor recovery from unexpected outcomes.
content:
arXiv:2610.15228v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Words are increasingly becoming an interface for action: large language models (LLMs) can now invoke tools, operate devices, and make decisions that affect the physical world. However, current benchmarks largely evaluate LLMs through static text responses, offline tool calls, or simulated tasks, leaving open the question of how well they can act in real physical environments. We present a benchmark for measuring LLMs in closed-loop physical interaction, where models control a harness system connected to real-world components including robotic arms, cameras, and sensors. In each task, the model must issue instructions, receive physical feedback from the environment, interpret the resulting state, and adapt its next action accordingly. This setting evaluates capabilities beyond language understanding, including grounded perception, action planning, tool selection, spatial reasoning, feedback-driven correction, and robustness to execution uncertainty. Through experiments with representative LLMs, we characterize their ability to translate linguistic reasoning into physical actions and identify common failure modes such as hallucinated state changes, poor recovery from unexpected outcomes, and unstable long-horizon plans. Our benchmark aims to provide a systematic foundation for evaluating LLMs as interactive agents that connect words, tools, and the physical world.

zh.title: 从言语到现实：在交互式物理环境中对大语言模型的基准测试
zh.summary: 介绍了第一个基准测试，用于评估大语言模型在与机械臂、摄像头和传感器的闭环物理交互中的表现，评估了超越基于文本能力的接地感知和实时适应。测试揭示了常见的故障模式，包括幻觉状态变化和对意外结果的恢复不良。

title: Using Evidence-Centered Design to Guide Prompt Engineering in Measurement: An Illustration with Automated Essay Scoring
summary: Proposes applying Evidence-Centered Design, an educational measurement framework, to structure prompt engineering for tasks like automated essay scoring, addressing validity threats from ad hoc approaches. Empirical results demonstrate that ECD-designed prompts improve validity, reliability, and fairness compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
content:
arXiv:2610.15231v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models, particularly large language models (LLMs), are increasingly used in educational settings for tasks such as item generation, automated scoring, and feedback delivery. The quality of these outputs depends not only on the AI model but also on how users construct the prompts that guide model behaviors. Current prompt engineering practices are largely ad hoc, relying on trial and error rather than principled design. This lack of structure introduces validity threats including construct misrepresentation, construct-irrelevant variance, and limited reproducibility. We propose that Evidence-Centered Design (ECD), a framework in educational measurement for structuring valid inferences from observed performance, can serve as a principled foundation for prompt engineering in educational applications. We map the three core ECD models, the student model, the evidence model, and the task model, onto the components of educational prompt design, and describe a workflow for ECD-based prompt engineering. We derive five design principles from this mapping and present an empirical study contrasting ECD-designed prompts with state-of-the-art (SOTA) prompting baselines on an automated scoring task. Our empirical study demonstrates the usefulness of this framework on automated scoring. Results suggest that treating prompting as assessment design rather than informal instructions strengthens the validity, reliability, and fairness of AI-generated educational outputs.

zh.title: 使用证据中心设计指导测量中的提示词工程：自动化论文评分示例
zh.summary: 提议应用证据中心设计（一个教育测量框架）来构建自动化论文评分等任务的提示词工程，解决临时方法带来的有效性威胁。实证结果表明，与最先进的基准相比，ECD设计的提示词提高了有效性、可靠性和公平性。

title: Why Static Skill Inconsistencies Do Not Equate to Runtime Risks: A Behavioral Analysis of LLM Agent Execution
summary: This paper studies the actual runtime impact of inconsistencies in skill packages used by LLM agents. Through auditing 575 skills and testing with 49 agent tasks, the research shows that static defect volume doesn't reliably predict runtime performance degradation, providing practitioners with evidence-based guidance on assessing real-world risks.
content:
arXiv:2610.18927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agent frameworks heavily rely on external skill assets to standardize tool usage, encode operational workflows, and supply executable runtime resources. Despite their widespread adoption, multi-component skill packages frequently suffer from cross-artifact inconsistencies, where documentation, scripts, and configuration files specify conflicting behavioral constraints. Although static auditing techniques can uncover such contractual discrepancies, static defect volume cannot reliably reflect real-world agent performance degradation. This gap leaves practitioners without rigorous evidence to assess the practical risk of flawed agent skills.
  This paper presents a systematic empirical study to demystify the runtime implications of skill inconsistencies. We conduct large-scale auditing over 575 community and benchmark skills, yielding 1,182 manually validated contract inconsistencies. We further build a controlled evaluation pipeline with 49 executable agent tasks and three representative LLMs across NoSkill, OriginalSkill, and FixedSkill experimental settings. Through fine-grained behavioral analysis of 441 paired execution trajectories, we quantify the actual performance impacts of resolved defects.

zh.title: 为什么静态技能不一致不等同于运行时风险：LLM代理执行的行为分析
zh.summary: 本论文研究了LLM代理使用的技能包中不一致性的实际运行时影响。通过审计575个技能并测试49个代理任务，该研究表明静态缺陷数量不能可靠地预测运行时性能退化，为从业者提供了评估真实世界风险的循证指导。

title: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
summary: This paper presents a system that enables human researchers to conduct computational research alongside AI coding agents through a distributed pipeline spanning task drafting, idea generation, planning, experimentation, and report writing. The system achieved scientific discovery across machine learning and demonstrated acceptance at ALIFE 2026, showing how multi-agent orchestration enables reliable scientific autonomy.
content:
arXiv:2610.18933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern coding agents are fundamentally reshaping the role of human input for computational research: they write code, launch in silico experiments, analyze their results, and autonomously operate with ever-increasing time horizons. Despite these developments, fully autonomous research agents suffer from a limited ideation radius and myopic hill-climbing search dynamics. To bridge this gap, we introduce The Agentic Scientist, an end-to-end distributed pipeline for human researchers to conduct computational research alongside modern coding agents. Building on its predecessor, our system decomposes research into task drafting, idea generation, planning, sandboxed experimentation, result aggregation, baseline and ablation construction, post-hoc analysis, and report writing. Importantly, each step in the pipeline is powered by the next generation of coding agents and leverages agentic self-verification. The overall research process is driven by a meta-controller that manages parallel research agents and enforces rubric verification at each stage. This design enables the same orchestration layer to be reused across heterogeneous domains with different execution environments, agentic coding harnesses, and evaluation metrics. Our system can be used across a spectrum of autonomy: either as a co-scientist tool or to perform end-to-end scientific investigation. Within the co-scientist setting, we leveraged a development version of our system to submit a single research paper, which got accepted for publication at ALIFE 2026. We further apply The Agentic Scientist fully autonomously to open problem-solving tasks in machine learning, and demonstrate the system's capability of scientific discovery across different domains of computational research. Our ablations suggest that reliable scientific autonomy depends not only on base model capabilities, but also on the cross-agent orchestration layer.

zh.title: 代理科学家：为自动化科学发现编排编码代理
zh.summary: 本论文介绍了一个系统，使研究人员能够通过跨越任务草拟、想法生成、规划、实验和报告撰写的分布式管道与AI编码代理一起进行计算研究。该系统在机器学习领域实现了科学发现，并获得ALIFE 2026的认可，展示了多代理编排如何实现可靠的科学自主性。

title: Beyond Equation Search: Conjecture-Guided Discovery with SCOPE and ClosureBench
summary: This paper shifts scientific discovery from optimizing individual equations to developing and testing conjectures that guide them. It introduces SCOPE framework for multi-agent conjecture-driven research and ClosureBench benchmark with 60 closure-discovery tasks, proposing metrics beyond equation accuracy including evidence faithfulness and experimental effectiveness.
content:
arXiv:2610.18938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most symbolic regression methods optimize candidate equations, but improving an equation's fit does not establish whether its underlying scientific conjecture should be retained, revised, or rejected. A conjecture may admit multiple mathematical realizations, and similarly accurate equations may imply different explanations. This motivates a shift from refining individual expressions to developing and testing the conjectures that guide them. We introduce SCOPE, a framework that sustains multiple conjecture-driven research trajectories. Multiple scientist agents independently pursue conjectures through equation modeling, question formulation, and active experimentation, then exchange evidence to revise their conjectures and research directions. Their findings are consolidated into a scientific report linking models, conclusions, and evidence. Existing equation-discovery benchmarks primarily assess recovered expressions, leaving the evidence and scientific conclusions established through the investigation underexamined. We therefore introduce ClosureBench, an interactive benchmark of 60 closure-discovery tasks across five scientific domains. ClosureBench focuses on closure-discovery tasks to give equation discovery a concrete scientific purpose. Each task embeds an unknown algebraic relation in a known PDE system, where agents control experimental conditions in OpenFOAM to acquire new data for equation discovery. Beyond equation accuracy, ClosureBench proposes three metrics to evaluate the discovery process: evidence faithfulness, mechanism insight, and experimental effectiveness. Compared with diverse baselines, SCOPE achieves higher equation accuracy on both ClosureBench and a real-world scientific discovery case, while producing more accurate, reliable, and effective scientific discoveries.

zh.title: 超越方程搜索：使用SCOPE和ClosureBench进行猜想引导的发现
zh.summary: 本论文将科学发现从优化单个方程转变为开发和测试指导它们的猜想。它介绍了用于多代理猜想驱动研究的SCOPE框架和包含60个闭包发现任务的ClosureBench基准，提出了超越方程精度的指标，包括证据保真度和实验有效性。

title: Discovering Undisclosed Concepts in LoRA Adapters for Diffusion-Based AIGC Models
summary: This paper addresses moderation risks in LoRA adapters by developing a method to discover undisclosed concepts they were trained to generate. The two-stage framework combines subspace-guided evolutionary search and paired visual identification to efficiently identify unknown concepts in text-to-image LoRA adapters.
content:
arXiv:2610.18990v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has made diffusion model personalization affordable and widely shareable, but it also creates moderation risks when harmful or problematic content is not faithfully disclosed. Hence, it is desired to develop a mechanism that, given a LoRA adapter, discovers the concept it was trained to generate, so as to support downstream investigation. We characterize the target concept through the conditioning input that most clearly exposes what the LoRA has learned. Such an input should induce coherent LoRA outputs that are distinctive from those of the base model and strongly align with the learned LoRA subspace. We therefore formulate concept discovery as searching for the conditioning input that jointly maximizes output coherence, LoRA-induced distinctiveness, and subspace alignment. Even with a clear objective, however, optimizing it over an open-ended input space is prohibitively expensive, since reliable evaluation of coherence and distinctiveness requires repeated diffusion rendering. Crucially, we observe that an input need not be rendered to determine whether it is promising. Its alignment with the learned LoRA subspace provides a lightweight signal for localizing promising candidates before visual verification. Based on this insight, we develop a two-stage framework for text-to-image LoRAs. Subspace-Guided Evolutionary Search (SGES) uses render-free subspace alignment to explore candidate prompts and retain a compact shortlist, while Paired Visual Identification (PVI) renders only these candidates and compares the LoRA and base-model outputs to identify those exhibiting coherent and distinctive generation behavior. This design enables efficient and reliable discovery of previously unknown concepts encoded in LoRA adapters.

zh.title: 在基于扩散的AIGC模型的LoRA适配器中发现未公开的概念
zh.summary: 本文通过开发方法来发现LoRA适配器中的未公开概念，解决了其审核风险。该两阶段框架结合子空间引导的进化搜索和配对视觉识别，以高效识别文本到图像LoRA适配器中的未知概念。

title: Smart Alone, Blind Together: Why Accuracy Fails to CertifyTheory of Mind in Multi-Agent Teams
summary: This paper argues that accuracy alone is an insufficient metric for certifying multi-agent coordination capabilities, as error dependencies and deployment costs determine practical risk. Testing with Hanabi and Level-Based Foraging tasks and five language models, it proposes the Blind-Spot Gate that prices error costs and measured dependence without deploying the module.
content:
arXiv:2610.19051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coordinators that act on what they infer about teammates are usually certified by the accuracy of those inferences. We argue that accuracy is the wrong certificate, for two reasons. First, the accuracy needed to act depends on what a wrong action costs, so the bar belongs to the deployment, not the module. Second, a module's errors are rarely independent, and dependence has a sign: positively associated errors help where their damage overlaps and hurt where it compounds, so an accuracy threshold fails in a predictable direction, and once wrong beliefs interact and can do harm, no rule based on accuracy is right for every module. We test these predictions in task assignment, Level-Based Foraging and Hanabi, with injected errors, trained and Bayesian modules and five language models, and in human judgments. Accuracy fails in both directions, approving harmful language-model deployments in Hanabi, where shared errors compound, and rejecting beneficial ones in task assignment, where costly errors are rare. In our tasks it also buys far less redundancy than independence predicts: from GPT-5.4-mini to Claude Opus 5.5, error on teammates the models have evidence about falls from 32% to 11%, but the chance that all three observers misread one falls only from 16% to 9% (independence: 3.4% to 0.15%). We propose certifying the deployment, with a Blind-Spot Gate that prices error costs, pairwise interactions and measured dependence without deploying the module. On held-out data from the cells it was developed on, it makes no significant false approval in 20 splits (accuracy: 3.2 per split), and in preregistered tests on modules it was not developed on, it recovers what accuracy rejects (seven classifiers: regret 0.004 against 0.479) and catches what accuracy approves (a Bayesian module: significant false approvals in 17 of 20 splits for accuracy, 1 for the gate).

zh.title: 聪慧独处，盲目齐心：为什么精度不能证明多智能体团队的心理理论
zh.summary: 本文论证准确性单独作为多智能体协调能力的指标是不充分的，因为错误依赖性和部署成本决定了实际风险。通过Hanabi和基于级别锻造任务与五个语言模型的测试，提出了盲点门框架，该框架对错误成本定价，并在不部署模块的情况下测量依赖性。

title: RLPE: Teaching LLMs to Prompt with Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces Reinforcement Learned Prompt Engineering (RLPE), which trains a model to write prompts by analyzing traces of a separate task model's failures. A 9B-parameter model trained with RLPE generates better prompts than frontier models and optimizers on 2/3 benchmarks, and the capability to iterate on prompts emerges without explicit training.
content:
arXiv:2610.19062v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Prompting is a widely used method for adapting general-purpose LLMs to domain-specific tasks. Effective prompts can be tedious to create manually, so prompt writing is increasingly handed to LLMs, with recent work training LLMs to write prompts for other models. These techniques either write prompts without observing how the task model behaves, blind to the failure modes the prompt should address, or must run alongside the task LLM at inference time, adding overhead to every query. Neither reflects how prompt engineering is often practiced. To close this gap, we introduce Reinforcement Learned Prompt Engineering (RLPE), which trains a model to analyze traces of a separate task model and write a prompt targeting the failures it observes. RLPE rewards the trained model strictly on prompt performance, so it learns the prompting strategies that improve the task model. The prompt is generated once and reused across the task, so inference does not require the trained model. Since RLPE needs only query access to the model it prompts, it is also compatible with closed-source models. We apply RLPE to Enigmata, BIG-Bench Extra Hard, and PlanBench. We train a 9B-parameter model that writes better prompts than state-of-the-art frontier models (gpt-5.6-sol and claude-opus-5) and prompt optimizers (GEPA and TextGrad) on 2/3 benchmarks. Although the model is never explicitly trained to iterate on prompts, this capability emerges at a level that matches or beats frontier models. The learned prompting capability also generalizes, with the trained model improving task models 6x larger than the one it trained with, including ones from entirely different model families, and matching claude-opus-5 on a fourth benchmark held out from training.

zh.title: RLPE：用强化学习教LLMs进行提示
zh.summary: 本文介绍强化学习提示工程（RLPE），通过分析任务模型失败的跟踪来训练模型编写提示。经RLPE训练的9B参数模型在2/3个基准上生成的提示优于最先进模型和优化器，而且无需显式训练就能出现迭代提示的能力。

title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
summary: This paper compares Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP) and Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigms for tool discovery in LLM agents across a dataset of 46,984 APIs. It finds a complexity-dependent crossover where RtP outperforms on simple queries while PtR excels on multi-tool queries, with implications for inference cost and routing strategies.
content:
arXiv:2610.19068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. Evaluating on ToolBench (46,984 unique API endpoints, 50 categories) across single-tool (G1), intra-category multi-tool (G2), and cross-category multi-tool (G3) query subsets, we find a clear complexity-dependent crossover: RtP outperforms PtR on single-tool queries while PtR outperforms RtP on multi-tool queries. This crossover holds at every retrieval budget (k=1 to 20), is robust across registry sizes from 1k to 47k APIs, and is consistent across model families (Gemini 2.5 Flash and gpt-oss-120b). We characterize a stub-hallucination failure mode (the LLM invents plausible but non-existent API names) that acts as a double-edged sword: on simple queries PtR's stubs abstract away proper-noun signals that RtP matches directly, yet on complex queries the same mechanism decomposes multi-faceted intent into functional sub-needs. We further analyze token overhead and show that PtR's extra discovery call roughly doubles inference cost, which pays off on multi-tool queries but hurts on single-tool ones, motivating complexity-adaptive routing as a practical direction, one that can be driven by a zero-cost signal already present in the pipeline (RtP's top-1 retrieval score).

zh.title: 优先规划还是检索？工具发现架构的规模研究
zh.summary: 本论文在46,984个API的数据集上比较了LLM代理工具发现中的检索后规划(RtP)和规划后检索(PtR)范式。研究发现了复杂度相关的交叉点，其中RtP在简单查询上表现更优，而PtR在多工具查询上表现更好，对推理成本和路由策略具有重要启示。

title: GroundGUI: GUI Grounding by High-Quality Data and Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces ScreenRef, a 586K-screenshot GUI grounding dataset across desktop, web, and mobile domains, and proposes D2RL method combining supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning. GroundGUI-8B achieves strong performance on multiple benchmarks while being competitive with models trained on closed-source data.
content:
arXiv:2610.19100v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Constructing robust GUI agents relies on multimodal visual grounding: the ability to precisely map natural language intents to actionable on-screen components. Despite abundant desktop, web, and mobile benchmarks, high-fidelity resources tailored for diverse environments are surprisingly scarce. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Screen Referring Grounding Dataset (ScreenRef), a comprehensive GUI grounding dataset consisting of GUI screenshots paired with natural language referring expressions and box or point annotations. Spanning desktop, web, and mobile domains, ScreenRef comprises 586K screenshots and over 633K referring expression instances, covering tasks such as text recognition, visual matching, spatial understanding, and refusal scenarios. To boost the model's grounding performance, we propose the Distillation-to-Reinforcement Learning (D2RL) method to address the limited generalization of supervised fine-tuning and the sparse reward problem in reinforcement learning. Utilizing ScreenRef, we train Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct via sequential SFT and D2RL training, yielding GroundGUI-8B. GroundGUI-8B achieves 95.2% on ScreenSpot-V2, 63.9% on ScreenSpot-Pro, 65.4% on OSWorld-G, 86.8% on MMBench-GUI L2, and 38.3% on UI-Vision. Among 8B-scale models, it produces substantial gains over models trained on open-source datasets, with performance comparable or even superior to models trained on closed-source data. Code, models, and datasets are available at https://github.com/PrentisAI/GroundGUI.

zh.title: GroundGUI：通过高质量数据和蒸馏强化学习进行GUI接地
zh.summary: 本论文介绍了ScreenRef数据集，包含586K个跨桌面、网络和移动领域的截图，用于GUI接地任务，并提出了结合监督微调与强化学习的D2RL方法。GroundGUI-8B在多个基准测试上实现强劲性能，与使用闭源数据训练的模型具有竞争力。

title: Plant Memory: Technical Language Processing and a Verified Maintenance Ontology for Agent-Accessible Failure Knowledge from SAP PM Work Orders
summary: This paper presents Plant Memory, a system applying technical language processing to maintenance work orders to build an ISO 14224-aligned ontology accessible to both humans and AI agents. On a synthetic dataset, the rule-based extraction achieves 96.2% component accuracy and 82.1% diagnostic accuracy, demonstrating how verified knowledge systems preserve expert maintenance knowledge.
content:
arXiv:2610.19131v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Maintenance work orders are the largest written record of how industrial equipment fails, yet in most plants they are close to unusable for analysis. Short texts are abbreviated and misspelt, asset identity is buried in free text, work-type labels contradict the work described, and the fields that matter most for reliability (symptom, root cause, action taken) are usually empty. As a result, diagnostic knowledge stays with senior technicians and leaves when they do. We present Plant Memory, a system that applies technical language processing (TLP) to SAP Plant Maintenance (PM) exports and builds an ISO 14224-aligned maintenance ontology in which every extracted statement is a reified fact carrying a confidence score, the evidence it was read from, and a verification state. Extraction is rule-first, with an optional large language model (LLM) acting as a second reader whose disagreements raise a fact's review priority rather than overwrite it. Technicians verify facts through a review queue, answer targeted knowledge-gap questions where failures repeat without a recorded cause, and approve or reject ontology drift proposals when new terms appear. The resulting graph is served to people through a web application and to AI agents through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, so both query the same verified knowledge and every answer cites the work orders behind it. On a synthetic 12-month export of 400 work orders from a parboiled-rice plant, rule-based extraction reaches 96.2% component accuracy, 88.9% failure-mode accuracy and 100% root-cause precision at 62% coverage; on 28 diagnostic questions, ranked root causes from the ontology are correct at top-1 in 82.1% of cases against 53.6% for the raw SAP root-cause column.

zh.title: Plant Memory：技术语言处理与验证维护本体——来自SAP PM工作单的代理可访问故障知识
zh.summary: 本论文介绍了Plant Memory系统，该系统对维护工作单应用技术语言处理，构建符合ISO 14224标准、人类与AI代理均可访问的本体。在合成数据集上，基于规则的抽取实现了96.2%的组件准确度和82.1%的诊断准确度，展示了验证知识系统如何保存专家维护知识。

title: Graph-Based Orchestration of Heterogeneous AI Models: A Control Node Approach to Composite Intelligence
summary: This paper presents a graph-based framework for orchestrating multiple AI techniques including planning, machine learning, constraint programming, and language models. Using directed acyclic graphs and behavior trees with specialized control nodes, the approach enables composite systems that leverage strengths of diverse models within a unified operational schema.
content:
arXiv:2610.19136v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a graph-based framework for Composite AI systems that integrate multiple AI techniques to address complex problems. We describe an architecture using specialized control nodes to orchestrate diverse models including planning, machine learning, constraint programming, and large language models. The system employs directed acyclic graphs and behavior trees to manage model relationships and execution sequencing. Our methodology encompasses data connectors, computational services, and a containerized deployment framework supporting hierarchical, sequential, and concurrent model composition patterns. Through case studies, we demonstrate how this architecture enables the creation of composite systems that leverage the strengths of multiple AI techniques within a unified operational schema, overcoming the limitations of single-model approaches.

zh.title: 异构AI模型的图基调度：复合智能的控制节点方法
zh.summary: 本文提出了一个图基框架，用于编排多种AI技术，包括规划、机器学习、约束编程和语言模型。该方法使用有向无环图和具有专门控制节点的行为树，支持复合系统在统一的操作架构中发挥多种模型的优势。

title: Compiling Expert Procedures into Verified Programs: When a Small Model Is Enough
summary: This paper demonstrates that an agentic verification architecture can make 8B-parameter models viable for procedural domains by compiling expert traces into verified programs. On retail and telecom benchmarks, small models reach 91.2% task completion when paired with verification, achieving comparable results to frontier models without fine-tuning.
content:
arXiv:2610.19148v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In procedural tool-use domains, how much of the gap between base models is procedure rather than capability? We build an explicit program from a teacher's traces and run it in front of unchanged small models, including an 8B model. The construction, PLVR , takes the reasoning traces of a teacher, Kimi-K3, clusters their segments to locate recurring operations, has a frontier model author one typed primitive per operation, each run by a small frozen model and assembles the program by A* search over a mined rule library, under a reference-action objective. At inference the program takes one of two forms: for troubleshooting and tool search it produces the chain of thought the student would otherwise generate for itself, and the student acts on it; for multi-turn tool matching the student proposes each action and the program checks, repairs, or retries it before it goes out. On the official tau2-Bench Retail and Telecom test sets and on LiveMCPBench, with three Nemotron base models and the same program for each, the answer depends on the domain. On Telecom, Granite-4.2-8B as the student goes from 43.0% to 91.2% under the program, and every Nemotron student reaches 93.3-94.4%, against at most 58.2% for fine-tuning on the same traces, prompt optimisation of the student, or two token-matched baselines. With Granite-4.2-8B as the student, the program is within 2 to 3 points of the Nemotron students on Telecom and within 3 on Retail, and 3 to 13 points below them on LiveMCPBench: where the domain is procedural an 8B student is enough, and on tool search the student still matters. On Retail and LiveMCPBench the program is competitive with the best baseline. The spread between base models shrinks from about 7 points to about 2, averaged over the suites, with no weights changed.

zh.title: 将专家程序编译为已验证的程序：小模型何时足够
zh.summary: 本文证明了代理验证架构可以通过将专家跟踪编译为已验证程序来使8B参数模型在程序领域可行。在零售和电信基准上，小模型与验证配对时达到91.2%的任务完成率，在无微调的情况下获得与前沿模型相当的结果。

title: AgentCIScope: Grounded Contextual Integrity Evaluation for LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces AgentCIScope, a benchmark for evaluating whether LLM agents preserve contextual integrity when accessing sensitive data across applications. Testing 12 agents on 936 realistic tasks reveals leakage rates from 32.5% to 94.4%, with significant variation across data types and environments, highlighting privacy risks in agent deployments.
content:
arXiv:2610.19158v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are becoming increasingly capable of handling daily workspace tasks by interacting with application environments through tool calls. However, as agents read and write sensitive user data across email, documents, and other applications, a central privacy question is whether they preserve contextual integrity (CI), that is, whether the information flows they produce comply with context-specific disclosure constraints. Existing work either focuses on model-level privacy leakage or evaluates agents in limited application environments with manually constructed disclosure constraints. In this work, we introduce AgentCIScope, a unified platform and benchmark for evaluating agent-level contextual integrity through executable, multi-step tasks across diverse, realistic application environments. AgentCIScope transforms public and synthetic privacy cases into executable agent tasks, with disclosure constraints grounded in three criteria: governing privacy policies, persona-based agreement, and a predefined sensitive-attribute taxonomy. Based on AgentCIScope, we evaluate 12 agents on 936 tasks and find that strong task-completion capability does not guarantee contextual-integrity preservation: single-run leakage rates range from 32.5% to 94.4%, while repeating each task five times further increases leakage by 4-19 percentage points. Leakage varies substantially across attributes: personal preferences and booking details have average leakage rates of 84.7% and 76.5%, compared with 17.1% for credit-card information and 29.4% for SSNs; environments: calendar has the highest average leakage rate as an information source, while WhatsApp ranks highest as an information destination; and governing privacy policies. AgentCIScope provides deep insights into agent privacy leakage and serves as a unified testbed for developing privacy-preserving agents.

zh.title: AgentCIScope：LLM代理的基础上下文完整性评估
zh.summary: 本文介绍了AgentCIScope，一个用于评估LLM代理在跨应用访问敏感数据时是否保持上下文完整性的基准。对12个代理进行936个现实任务测试表明泄漏率从32.5%到94.4%不等，在不同数据类型和环境中存在显著差异，突出了代理部署中的隐私风险。

title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
summary: This benchmark evaluates whether AI agents can advance open scientific problems by writing follow-up papers guided by domain scientists from US Department of Energy labs. Of 135 submissions from nine frontier agents, none satisfied all conditions and 114 failed integrity checks, indicating substantial headroom for improvement in autonomous scientific research.
content:
arXiv:2610.19159v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can AI agents carry out research on open scientific problems? We introduce Into the Unknown, a benchmark that provides an agent with a science paper along with a research direction to pursue and tasks it to write a follow-up paper. We work with scientists at US Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratories, who each contribute an unpublished follow-up direction from their own work together with the necessary conditions a submission must meet. While assessing the quality of a follow-up paper is challenging in general, using these conditions to form a rubric makes evaluation more tractable for research problems that have no reference answer. We have nine frontier agents write 15 follow-ups each, spanning quantum computing, plasma physics, computational chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning domains. None of the 135 submissions satisfies all the conditions, and 114 fail our integrity check, most often because the paper claims work that was never done or reports numbers that contradict the recorded evidence. Overall, agents readily produce papers that look like follow-ups, but none meets the standard of the domain scientist, leaving substantial headroom. Our code and data are publicly available.

zh.title: 迈向未知：在开放科学研究问题上对AI代理的基准测试
zh.summary: 这项基准测试评估了AI代理是否能够在美国能源部实验室领域科学家的指导下撰写后续论文来推进开放科学问题。在来自九个前沿代理的135份提交中，没有任何一个满足所有条件，114份未通过完整性检查，表明自主科学研究有很大的改进空间。

title: ListQA: A Benchmark for Evaluating List-Formatted Factual Knowledge Retrieval in Large Language Models
summary: ListQA is a benchmark of 9,045 human-curated questions requiring LLMs to retrieve and organize multiple facts into structured lists across eight categories. Evaluating 34 models, the research shows even the best achieves below 37% accuracy, and models struggle to retrieve facts from parameters alone despite successfully organizing provided information.
content:
arXiv:2610.19165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many real-world questions demand not a single fact but an organized collection of them, yet existing factual knowledge benchmarks almost exclusively target single answer retrieval. We introduce ListQA, a benchmark of 9,045 human-curated, cross-validated questions (audited error rate of 1.7%) that require LLMs to recall multiple facts and compose them into structured lists of 3-10 elements. Questions range from flat lists ("Which NCAA teams went undefeated between 2000 and 2024?") to hierarchical lists with sub-attributes ("...and what was their record and result?"), spanning eight categories across 60+ countries. An evergreen design (explicit temporal constraints or historically immutable facts) keeps ground truth valid without periodic updates. For evaluation, we frame element matching as a linear sum assignment problem: optimal bipartite matching paired with LLM-based semantic grading jointly captures factual accuracy, hallucination, and format compliance. We benchmark 34 models (8 families, 42 configurations across standard and thinking enabled inference) and find: the best standard-inference model scores below 37% LLM-Judge-F1, multi-faceted questions are harder across the board, and providing the source Wikipedia page lifts scores dramatically, confirming that models can organize facts but struggle to retrieve them from parameters alone. Extended analyses cover base vs. instruction-tuned checkpoints and token efficiency. We release the dataset and evaluation code.

zh.title: ListQA：评估大型语言模型列表格式事实知识检索的基准
zh.summary: ListQA是一个包含9,045个人工精选问题的基准，要求大型语言模型检索并将多个事实组织成八个类别的结构化列表。对34个模型的评估研究表明，即使是表现最好的模型准确度也低于37%，模型难以仅从参数中检索事实，尽管它们能成功组织提供的信息。

title: Verification Turns Capability Gaps into Routing Decisions: Small Language Models for Clinical Documentation
summary: This paper shows that agentic verification architecture enables a 4B-parameter model to generate clinical notes with 0.984 factual entailment, comparable to frontier models. A verification-based routing policy routes 62 cases to the frontier model while handling 75% on-device, achieving 99.6% verified acceptance and demonstrating how verification can overcome capability gaps.
content:
arXiv:2610.19169v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical note generation from doctor--patient dialogue is high-volume and hallucination-intolerant: a fabricated laboratory value can create patient-safety risk, not a quality regression. We ask whether an agentic \emph{verification} architecture, rather than generator scale, can make a small language model viable here. Holding a four-evaluator verification stack and refinement policy fixed and swapping only the generator between a 4B-parameter model with a QLoRA adapter and a frontier baseline, the small model reaches $0.984$ claim-level factual entailment against $0.992$ and comes within $3.3$ points on completeness, generating entirely on-device. Its deficit is confined to \emph{inter-section structural fidelity}---arrangement rather than clinical comprehension, and the axis on which it also falls furthest below the corpus's reference notes. Because that deficit is an explicit verifier decision rather than a silent quality difference, it becomes a routing policy: run the small model by default, escalate what the verifier rejects. Measured end to end, that it achieved a similiar verified-rate acceptance to the frontier-only acceptance in this test set ($99.6\%$ vs.\ $98.4\%$ over $250$ encounters) while routing $62$, documenting three quarters without a frontier \emph{generation} call. Ablating the loop separates architecture from scale: unrefined, the small model is accepted on $26.8\%$ of encounters and the frontier model on $74.8\%$, so verification does the most work where the generator is weakest. We also contribute section-scoped refinement, which preserves unflagged sections by construction rather than instruction, and find the baseline is not uniformly stronger---its provider refused two trauma-related transcripts the on-device model handled and certified, one facet of a provider dependency a served adapter does not carry.

zh.title: 验证将能力差距转化为路由决策：用于临床文档的小型语言模型
zh.summary: 本文表明代理验证架构使4B参数的模型能够生成具有0.984事实蕴含的临床笔记，与前沿模型相当。基于验证的路由策略将62个案例路由到前沿模型，同时处理75%的设备端任务，实现99.6%的验证接受率，展示了验证如何克服能力差距。
